rationale: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=200, epochs=40, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, uswin_c=32, swin_window=8, swin_heads=8, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=ITER-11. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) READ iter-1..10: hr .649/.8193/.8092/.8208/.8136/.8093/.8440(c24bs1)/.8464(c32bs1,BEST)/.8289(c48)/.8378(c32bs1 ep64->backstop ep37). iter-10 tried epochs 40->64 but ran on a SLOWER node (~27s/ep vs iter-8's ~18s/ep), so the max_train_s=1000 backstop capped it at ep37 < iter-8's 40 -> it tested FEWER epochs, not more (confound). hr 0.8378 at 37ep vs 0.8464 at 40ep is consistent with the monotone epochs->hr relation. LEARNING: at c32/bs1 the run must actually reach >=40 epochs to hit ~0.846; node contention that trips the backstop early costs hr. Epochs lever is real but the wall-clock backstop + variable node speed make it unreliable. (2) FAILURE MODE / limiter: to be ROBUST to node-speed variance I need to reach the good basin in FEWER epochs. The untested lever in the NEW c32/bs1 regime is the OPTIMIZATION STEP SIZE. iter-1..10 at c32/bs1 all used lr=2e-4 (inherited from the bs2 era); bs1 has 2x update density so its lr dynamics differ from bs2. iter-5's lr=4e-4 test was at bs2 (stale regime). (3) ONE KNOB: lr 2e-4 -> 3e-4 (1.5x); hold everything else at iter-8 BEST (c32, bs=1, ep=40, win=8, heads=8, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). BUDGET-NEUTRAL (same per-epoch cost, same ep40 target). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a 1.5x-larger lr reaches the convergence basin in FEWER epochs (making hr robust to backstop/node-speed variance) AND possibly a marginally better minimum, lifting hr toward/above 0.8464. grad_clip=1.0 guards a spike; bs1's dense low-variance gradients tolerate a higher lr than bs2 did. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.8464 (flat) or drops/destabilizes at lr=3e-4, the c32/bs1/lr2e-4/ep40 config (iter-8, 0.8464) is the robust optimum -> iter-12 probes train_n 200->400 (more data; accepts the backstop epoch-cut) or a cosine lr schedule. (5) 20-min budget via max_train_s=1000 backstop; val_n=200; expandable_segments OOM-guard. (6) STRICT SERIAL: rm iter-11 obs pre-dispatch; iter_wait.sh gate before iter-12.
